clue.text: The cards might be made stiffer

definitions.text: The cards might be made stiffer

parts.words: The cards might be made stiffer
parts.note: cards here are shirt collars and cuffs, or a stiff old-fashioned person, treated with laundry stiffener; the clue reads like a card trick

explanation.surface: A remark about stiffening a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry stiffener applied to linen or card makes it rigid, so stiffened cards are treated this way.

clue.text: Writing up about cold man's separation

indicators.note: about means the reversed writing goes around the other letters
in a down clue, up means the word for writing is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a man's belongings are his

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a cold man splitting from others.
explanation.definitionFit: A split into opposed factions, especially in a church, is a separation.

clue.text: Medication needed in a car smash

indicators.note: a smash wrecks things, so the letters of the words before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hurt in a car crash needs treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal remedy rubbed on bruises, made from a mountain plant, is a medication.

clue.text: Amusing yet firm male in charge

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm man in charge who is somehow funny too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something funny or laughable is amusing, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Chapter and verse after record is set

indicators.note: after places the verse later than the record and is, so it comes at the end

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A book chapter and its verse are set down after a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link word here, meaning the pieces are placed in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: One instalment in a series or story is like a chapter in a book.

clue.text: Note change given and hesitate

parts.note: F is a musical note, one of the letters naming the scale
to alter something is to change it

explanation.surface: A musical note is changed and someone wavers.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver or lose nerve is to hesitate.

clue.text: Serving minced meat and beans or humble pie

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up, so the letters of meat and beans are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A menu offering mince and beans, or a humble pie for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder words and gives no letters. To eat humble pie is to suffer humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating humble pie means accepting humiliation, the state of being lowered in dignity.

clue.text: It's about a Latin fellow's charm

indicators.note: about means the short form of it is goes around the other letters

parts.note: 'tis is the old contracted form of it is
a man is a fellow; the 's links him to the charm

explanation.surface: Someone describes a Latin man's charming manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An object believed to bring luck or ward off harm is a lucky charm.

clue.text: Army personnel counted as discharged

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army personnel
to be deemed something is to be counted as it

explanation.surface: Soldiers regarded as having been released from service.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt or pledge paid off is discharged, as when goods are bought back from a pawnbroker.

clue.text: The manicurist?

parts.note: read literally, a manicurist is a female servant who attends to the hands

explanation.surface: A question about who does your nails.
explanation.definitionFit: A female servant is a maid; one tending hands could be called this, though it means any personal attendant.

clue.text: Lay feeling under the weather all in

indicators.note: in means the word all sits inside the word for feeling poorly

parts.note: to feel bad is to feel ill or under the weather
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly lies down completely exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a narrative song or poem.

clue.text: Could start with fruit and a morsel of fried food

indicators.note: the start of could is its opening letter

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Fruit could begin a plate of fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fried potato is a morsel of fried food.

clue.text: Wine church members find rough stuff

parts.note: sack is an old name for dry white wine such as sherry
the cloth means the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: Clergy discover that the communion wine is coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse fabric of goat hair or hemp worn as penance is rough stuff, stuff meaning cloth.

clue.text: Follow directions and engage in litigation

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
N is north, a compass direction
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A litigant follows instructions and goes to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a consequence is to follow.

clue.text: Material obtained from Central America

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fabric imported from Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiny fabric woven with metallic threads is a material.

clue.text: Cheered when a number made demands

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to have claimed is to have demanded something as a right

explanation.surface: A crowd cheered as someone pressed their demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Praised enthusiastically and publicly means much the same as applauded.

clue.text: Order quiet about cut

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
re means about or concerning
to pare is to trim or cut

explanation.surface: An order to keep quiet about a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange or make ready, as in ordering papers, is a sense of the verb.

clue.text: Poor actors accepting chaff as bedding

indicators.note: accepting means the word for bad actors takes the other word inside it

parts.note: hams are actors who overact
to chaff is to tease or mock

explanation.surface: Bad actors take teasing about their sleeping arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging beds of net or canvas, as on ships, are a form of bedding.

clue.text: The protection of cod takes organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of cod takes are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Protecting cod stocks needs proper management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The', 'of' are link words; a fishery picture hides the defence of posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier of upright stakes around a place is a defensive protection.

clue.text: Possibly the leader will make it clear

indicators.note: will make says the letters of it clear are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Perhaps the boss will explain things plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: 'the' is the definite article, and a leader is a newspaper's lead editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'the' is a grammatical article, and a newspaper leader is an opinion article.

clue.text: Eat out in Letchworth say

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the town name that follows

explanation.surface: Dining out in a Hertfordshire town, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Letchworth is a garden city in Hertfordshire, England; 'say' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid eats into metal to make a design, so eat out is the engraver's sense.

clue.text: A city club with aspiration

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
H is the breathy sound of aspiration in phonetics

explanation.surface: A city sports club with lofty ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa city in Somerset, England; aspiration is the breathed h-sound, not ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic spa town in the west of England is a city.

clue.text: Musicians require time for dressing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Musicians need time to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material wrapped around a wound is a dressing.

clue.text: Fit to be one of the boat-crew

explanation.surface: Healthy enough to row in the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure from blocked blood to the brain is a fit; in rowing the oarsman setting the pace is so named.

clue.text: As it may be said, no good-looker!

annotationWithheld.why: As it may be said, no good-looker! (6): no parse found for the wordplay before the definition good-looker; it may be a homophone pun but the words that sound out the answer cannot be identified.
annotationWithheld.clue: As it may be said, no good-looker!

clue.text: Coffee, or, if there's little time, tea

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A choice of coffee, or tea if you are in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong coffee from Arabia, often mixed with chocolate, is a type of coffee.

clue.text: Awfully decent-not relaxed though

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of decent and not are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone awful but not relaxed despite being decent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied and at ease means being relaxed.

clue.text: Appearing before the court without a list

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone appears in court without a list of charges.
explanation.walkthrough: A list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship, so 'without a list' means upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing straight with no tilt or lean is being upright.

clue.text: Sticky heavy soil contains thousands

indicators.note: contains means the word for heavy soil holds the other letters inside

parts.note: clay is a heavy, dense soil
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them are thousands

explanation.surface: Damp heavy soil holds thousands of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasantly damp and tacky to touch means sticky.

clue.text: Owner distracted after vehicle gets crushed

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled owner later than the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: distracted means confused, so the letters of owner are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distracted car owner gets flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn down and worried by troubles is how someone crushed by care looks.

clue.text: Showing craft about exercise, the top journalist runs

indicators.note: about means the craft letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft
PE is physical education, exercise
ED is the editor, the top journalist

explanation.surface: A showboating editor exercises before going for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Going fast, as a runner or engine does, means rushing along.

clue.text: Contact the head, all being right

parts.note: to meet someone is to contact them
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: Get in touch with the boss to check all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitability, the quality of being fitting or proper, is everything being right.
